question_text: If z = (cos θ, sin θ), find z − 1/z.

mark_split.label: Find 1/z as cos θ − i sin θ

recall_prompt: Say how you would find z minus one over z — what 1/z is for a cis value, and what is left after subtracting.
insider_note: The ordered pair (cos θ, sin θ) is the complex number cos θ + i sin θ, and because its modulus is 1 the reciprocal is simply the conjugate cos θ − i sin θ. Subtracting cancels the cos terms, so the answer is 2i sin θ — 2cos θ is z + 1/z, a different question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find 1/z
steps.margin_note: First mark. The ordered pair (cos θ, sin θ) is the complex number cos θ + i sin θ. Its reciprocal is found by the conjugate; since cos²θ + sin²θ = 1 the denominator is 1 and 1/z is simply cos θ − i sin θ.
lines: z = (cos θ, sin θ) = cos θ + i sin θ

recall.must_convey: That z = cos θ + i sin θ and 1/z = cos θ − i sin θ, because multiplying by the conjugate gives denominator cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.
accept: z is cos theta plus i sin theta and one by z is cos theta minus i sin theta because the denominator cos squared plus sin squared is one
the reciprocal of cis theta is cos theta minus i sin theta
multiply by the conjugate, the bottom is one, so one over z is cos theta minus i sin theta
one by z ante cos theta minus i sin theta, denominator one
one over z is the conjugate cos theta minus i sin theta
heard_as: cos theta minus i sin theta

steps.why: A cis value has modulus 1, so its reciprocal is its conjugate — no division is really needed. Writing the conjugate step once shows where cos θ − i sin θ comes from.
common_mistakes: Writing 1/z as 1/cos θ + 1/(i sin θ), splitting a fraction over a sum.
Leaving cos²θ + sin²θ in the denominator instead of replacing it by 1.

steps.label: Subtract
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The cos θ terms cancel; the sin θ terms add.
lines: z − 1/z = (cos θ + i sin θ) − (cos θ − i sin θ)

recall.must_convey: That subtracting cancels the cos θ terms and leaves 2i sin θ.
accept: subtract, cos theta cancels and i sin theta plus i sin theta is two i sin theta
z minus one by z equals two i sin theta
the cos terms cancel leaving two i sin theta
cos theta cancel ayyi two i sin theta vasthundi
the answer is two i sin theta

steps.why: z − 1/z = cis θ − cis(−θ) is purely imaginary, and equals 2i sin θ; the companion fact z + 1/z = 2cos θ is the one De Moivre questions use. Both come from the same reciprocal line.
common_mistakes: Dropping the i and answering 2 sin θ.
